desc:
iOS app integrations connect your iPhone app to payments, analytics and your own backend. Ecom Swift LLC sets up each service in your own accounts, builds the code in a clean module and tests it with test and live data, so the connections work in the real app.

## What are iOS app integrations?

iOS app integrations are the connections between your app and outside services: in-app purchases through StoreKit, analytics tools, push and email providers, error monitoring and your own API. Each connection moves data in one direction or both, and the app has to handle every case where that exchange fails.

Most of the work happens where the user cannot see it. Keys, tokens, request formats, retries and data mapping decide whether the feature simply works or fails once a week without anyone knowing why.

## Why integrations are easy to get wrong

Provider documentation shows the successful path. Real phones lose network in a lift, switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data, go to the background in the middle of a request and run old app versions for months. An integration that ignores these cases produces missing orders, duplicate charges, lost analytics and users who are signed out for no reason.

Keys add another risk. A secret key placed inside the app bundle can be extracted, and test keys left in a release build cause confusing failures. Careful setup keeps each key where it belongs.

## How integrations affect your business

Purchases decide whether the app earns revenue at all. Analytics tells you which screens people use and where they leave, so you can spend effort wisely. Push providers bring users back, and a backend connection keeps their data in sync across devices.

Without these links, the app is a standalone program. With them, it becomes part of how your business sells, learns and talks to customers.

## What a sound integration includes

- Separate test and live keys, stored in your own provider accounts.
- Secrets kept out of the app wherever possible, with server-side calls where required.
- A small, clean module for each service, so it can be replaced later.
- Error handling for failed, slow and repeated requests.
- Retry and offline behavior that does not duplicate actions.
- Analytics events with clear names and a written list of what each one means.
- StoreKit purchase and restore flows that follow Apple's rules.
- Push notification setup with your Apple keys and permission wording.
- Notes on how each connection works and which provider limits we met.

## What we do

We begin with a list of the services you want and what each should do. We read the provider's documentation, create the keys and settings in your accounts, then build the connection and test it with test data first. When it works, we repeat the checks with live settings.

Basic connects one service with short setup notes. Standard connects up to three services, adds analytics events, calls to your backend and retry handling. Premium covers a full set that can include StoreKit purchases, push notifications, backend sync and crash monitoring.

You receive working screens, the code and plain notes written for the next developer.

## Digital content and card payments

Apple has rules about how an app may charge for digital goods and services inside the app. Purchases of that kind usually have to use in-app purchase, while physical goods and some real-world services can use other payment providers. We build the flow that fits your product and tell you plainly when a requested setup may conflict with the App Review Guidelines.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Create accounts with each provider under your own business name.
- Share API documentation, even if it is rough.
- Test purchases with a sandbox account before going live.
- Keep a list of every service and key the app depends on.
- Plan what the app should do when a service is down.

**Avoid:**
- Putting secret keys directly in the app code.
- Adding analytics events for every tap.
- Skipping the restore purchases flow.
- Using one provider account shared across unrelated projects.
- Releasing without a test using live settings.

## Who this is for

A shop owner who wants a purchase flow and email receipts in the app can use this. So can a team with a ready backend that needs the iPhone side connected, and a product manager who wants analytics in place before a campaign starts.

## What we need from you

Tell us which services to connect and what each should do. We need access to the provider dashboards as a team member where the provider supports it, a collaborator invitation to the repository and the documentation for your backend. We never need your passwords. You pay each provider directly, as our price covers the connection work only.
